title: Telecoms, data centres target improved internet interconnection
summary: Telecom operators, ISPs and data centres will discuss stronger local internet exchange at a Lagos forum on 28–29 October 2026. Topics include peering and infrastructure.
body:
Telecommunications operators, internet service providers and data centre companies are expected to examine ways to strengthen domestic internet traffic exchange at a two-day forum in Lagos on 28 and 29 October 2026. The Nigerian Peering and Interconnection Forum is being convened by the Nigerian Network Operators Group, in collaboration with the Internet Exchange Point of Nigeria and the Nigerian Communications Commission.

The discussions will address internet peering and interconnection, local traffic exchange, data centre infrastructure, connectivity, content delivery, regional links and regulation. Network operators, content providers, technology companies, regulators and other participants in the digital infrastructure sector are expected to attend.

The focus comes amid growing use of the internet, cloud computing and digital services, which increases demand for reliable connectivity and efficient traffic exchange. When networks exchange traffic locally, rather than routing it through international networks, services may benefit from lower latency and more efficient delivery. The extent of those gains depends on infrastructure availability, network capacity, where data centres and content are located, and whether operators can agree on commercially viable arrangements.

Prof. Adewale Adedokun, convenor of the Nigerian Network Operators Group, said the forum would give stakeholders an opportunity to consider shared infrastructure challenges and develop practical responses. He has emphasised the need for cooperation among operators, data centres, content providers, regulators, internet exchange points and technology companies as demand for online services grows.

The programme is set to include research presentations, technical sessions, panel discussions and fireside conversations. Organisers say participants will consider how localising internet traffic, content and digital services could support network performance, resilience and efficiency, while also providing a forum to exchange technical knowledge and identify opportunities for collaboration and investment.

title: CBD COP17: Nigeria, six others each win $50,000 grant for biodiversity projects
summary: Nigeria and six other countries received $50,000 grants for projects supporting their 30×30 biodiversity targets. Nigeria’s project will be implemented by NCF.
body:
Nigeria and six other countries have each received a $50,000 seed grant for projects intended to advance their 30×30 conservation targets. The awards were announced on the sidelines of the 17th session of the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity in Armenia. The beneficiary countries are Costa Rica, Mexico, Nigeria, Nepal, Zambia, Rwanda and Kenya.

Nigeria’s grant will support a project on ecological connectivity, terrestrial and marine Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures (OECMs), and protected-area management effectiveness. The Nigerian Conservation Foundation (NCF) will implement the project. Its director-general, Joseph Onoja, said the foundation would work with the Federal Ministry of Environment to provide scientific and technical support.

The project is expected to identify and map priority terrestrial and marine OECMs, assess how effectively protected areas are managed, and develop a national framework for evaluating management effectiveness. The work is intended to produce evidence and recommendations to strengthen Nigeria’s protected and conserved areas and support implementation of Target 3 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. Nigeria’s biodiversity focal point, Sikeade Egbuwalo, said the funding could also help address fragmented habitats.

The other grants will support projects tailored to each country’s conservation priorities. They include improving visitor-management planning at Costa Rica’s Cocos Island National Park; developing underwater acoustic baselines for Mexico’s marine protected areas; recognising OECMs in Nepal; assessing Zambia’s Busanga Swamps; supporting community-based conservation and ecological connectivity in Rwanda; and advancing community-led marine conservation in Kenya.

The Rapid Deployment Mechanism, established by the High Ambition Coalition for Nature and People, provides small-scale funding intended to address financing gaps and help countries move early-stage conservation work forward. The organisers describe the grants as a way to bridge initial project needs and larger sources of funding. The 30×30 goal is to conserve at least 30 per cent of land and sea by 2030.

title: Okonjo-Iweala loses mother, as Tinubu mourns
summary: President Bola Tinubu has mourned Prof. Kamene Okonjo, who died aged 96, and extended condolences to her daughter Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala and the Ogwashi-Uku community.
body:
President Bola Tinubu has extended condolences to the Okonjo royal family of Ogwashi-Uku, Delta State, following the death of Prof. Kamene Okonjo, aged 96. He also expressed sympathy to her daughter, Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, director-general of the World Trade Organization, other relatives and members of the community.

Tinubu described Prof. Okonjo as an accomplished academic whose life was marked by intellectual distinction and service. He recognised her contributions to scholarship and her commitment to advancing women and society.

The president also praised her dedication to family and community, and her role in preserving traditional institutions. He offered prayers for her eternal rest and for comfort for her family and others mourning her death.

title: NDLEA arrests South African woman with 36.65kg of cocaine at Lagos airport
summary: NDLEA says it seized 36.65kg of cocaine from a South African woman at Lagos airport and arrested other suspects in separate drug operations.
body:
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency says it arrested a 34-year-old South African woman at Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos with 36.65kg of cocaine. Qhina Beauty was detained on October 7 as she prepared to board a Qatar Airways flight to South Africa via Doha. Officers found 30 blocks of cocaine in her two travel bags, concealed in seven parcels with dried pepper. The agency said she told investigators she had arrived in Nigeria on September 30 to collect the drugs.

Further inquiries led to the arrest of car dealer Uchenna Victor Umunnakwe, 46, on October 14 in Lagos. The agency said he admitted receiving Beauty at the airport, arranging her accommodation at two hotels and moving her to a hotel near the airport before her departure.

In a separate airport operation, officers arrested Anetor Gloria Ubong, a 62-year-old realtor based in Texas, after she arrived from Houston on October 21. A search of her checked luggage uncovered 18 parcels of cannabis known as loud, weighing 9.45kg and wrapped in gift paper. The agency said Ubong, who has Nigerian and US passports, told investigators the box had been given to her in the United States for delivery to her daughter’s fiancé in Nigeria.

The agency also reported seizures and arrests elsewhere. In Lagos, officers found diazepam and tramadol tablets, 3.7kg of skunk and 230.25 litres of a locally produced alcoholic-drug mixture called skuchies at the residence of 41-year-old Eletu Rasheedat. In Warri, Delta State, they arrested Peter Ugochukwu, 51, and seized thousands of tramadol capsules and tablets, codeine syrup, Rohypnol and other substances, including injectable drugs. A separate arrest in Warri led to the seizure of 6kg of skunk from Helen Bakporo Samson, 46.

In Ibadan, Oyo State, NDLEA operatives arrested Fajana Dada Oluwaseyi, 41. The agency said officers had previously seized 197.8kg of cannabis from his residence on September 16, after which he escaped arrest. The latest operations are part of the agency’s stated effort to disrupt drug trafficking and seize illicit substances across Nigeria.

title: Soldiers earn peanuts, APC youth leader flaunts billion-naira SUVs — Utomi
summary: Utomi criticised the APC after Dayo Israel displayed new Toyota Prado SUVs for selected youth leaders. He questioned the spending amid low soldier pay.
body:
Professor Pat Utomi has criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC) after its national youth leader, Dayo Israel, displayed new Toyota Prado SUVs that he said were presented to selected youth leaders. Utomi questioned the vehicles’ cost and the priorities behind the distribution, contrasting it with what he described as low salaries for Nigerian soldiers.

In a post on X on Sunday, Utomi said it was troubling that an APC youth leader was showing off expensive vehicles while Nigerians had been told government funds were limited. He wrote that soldiers were being paid “peanuts” and argued the situation could leave the public feeling they were being treated as fools.

Utomi also raised the possibility of using the money for other needs, particularly health services. He said each SUV in the video cost more than ₦100 million and asked how many “world-class ambulances” the expenditure could buy. The cost figure was presented by Utomi; the source material does not give an overall price for the vehicles or identify who paid for them.

Israel said the vehicles were intended to support election mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. In his post accompanying the video, he thanked First Lady Oluremi Tinubu for what he described as her continued support for the party’s structure under his leadership, and said the party would work to deliver “polling unit by polling unit.” The video has since been deleted. Its display prompted criticism on social media, including questions about the timing of the distribution amid economic hardship associated with the administration’s reforms. Utomi’s comments added to those concerns by focusing on public spending priorities.

title: Mbappe’s Brace Helps Real Madrid Beat Barcelona In La Liga Clasico
summary: Kylian Mbappe scored twice as Real Madrid beat Barcelona 2-1 at Camp Nou. The win cut Madrid’s gap to La Liga leaders Barcelona to three points.
body:
Kylian Mbappe scored twice as Real Madrid defeated Barcelona 2-1 at Camp Nou on Sunday, handing the La Liga leaders their first domestic loss of the campaign. The result cut Madrid’s gap to Barcelona to three points, although Madrid remain third behind Barcelona and Atletico Madrid. Raphinha scored Barcelona’s only goal, equalising after Mbappe had put the visitors ahead before half-time.

The opening half was tight, with Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi twice stopping Mbappe and Andriy Lunin making a save from Anthony Gordon. Madrid took the lead when Gerard Martin’s attempted clearance struck Mbappe and deflected into the net. Barcelona had a chance to respond before the break, but Lamine Yamal fired wide. Xavi Espart also had to leave the field injured before the half-hour mark, with Alejandro Balde coming on.

Barcelona improved after the interval and drew level just after the hour. Pedri set up Raphinha, who shot through Jude Bellingham’s legs; Lunin could not keep the effort out. The hosts then pressed for a second, but Lunin denied Martin and Yamal missed the target, while Dean Huijsen blocked a shot from substitute Frenkie de Jong.

Madrid struck late after substitute Gabriel Jesus lost possession. Eduardo Camavinga got past Cubarsi and squared the ball for Mbappe to score into an unguarded net, with Barcelona goalkeeper Joan Garcia out of position. It was Madrid’s fifth straight win across all competitions, while Barcelona suffered a second consecutive defeat following their Champions League loss to Paris Saint-Germain. Midfielder Pedri said Barcelona had not played well, particularly in the first half, but noted that the league season was long.

title: FULL LIST: NDC names Peter Obi, Henry Dickson, others as campaign council members
summary: The NDC named Henry Dickson chair and Peter Obi co-chair of its 2027 National Campaign Council. The appointments cover advisory, campaign and state roles.
body:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress has formed a National Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections, naming its National Leader, Senator Henry Dickson, as chairman and presidential candidate Peter Obi as co-chairman. The party announced the appointments in a statement posted on its X account on Sunday, saying the council would coordinate campaign activity nationwide and mobilise support for its vision of a “new, just, and prosperous Nigeria.”

The party’s National Chairman and vice-presidential candidate, Senator Cleopas Zuwoghe, was named vice-chairman, with Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso as co-vice-chairman. National Secretary Ikenna Enekweizu is among the council’s leadership, while Ibrahim Abdulkarim was named council secretary and director-general of the presidential campaign. Other listed council members include Babachir Lawal, Ovie Omo-Agege, Victor Umeh, Buba Galadima and Dudu Manuga.

The announcement also sets out a National Campaign Advisory Council, chaired by Lawal, with Zuwoghe as co-chairman and former governor Sam Egwu as vice-chairman. Its membership includes state representatives across the country, among them Pat Utomi, Oseloka Obaze, Onyema Ugochukwu and Achike Udenwa. The party also named campaign directorates covering areas such as finance, communications, logistics, policy, legal affairs, security, election monitoring, youth and women’s mobilisation, and diaspora engagement.

State campaign coordinators were appointed across the states and the Federal Capital Territory. The list includes Senator Nkechi Nwogu for Abia, Bamanga Tukur Jr. for Adamawa, Ken Pela for Delta, Ife Salako for Lagos and Stephen Knabayi for the FCT. The entries for Nasarawa and Niger identify the coordinators only as senatorial candidates, without giving names.

The NDC said the council would provide strategic leadership and drive a “people-centred and issue-based campaign.” It urged party members, supporters and Nigerians to remain united and focused ahead of the polls, adding that “a new and working Nigeria is possible.”

title: CBD COP17: Namibian Biosafety Expert Martha Kandawa-Schulz dies in Yerevan
summary: Namibian biosafety expert Martha Kandawa-Schulz died in Yerevan on 23 October while attending CBD COP17. She was co-chairing a conference working group.
body:
Namibian biosafety expert Martha Kandawa-Schulz died in Yerevan, Armenia, on 23 October while attending the United Nations Biodiversity Conference, known as CBD COP17. The Convention on Biological Diversity Secretariat announced her death in a statement issued on Sunday evening.

Kandawa-Schulz was Namibia’s Cartagena Protocol National Focal Point and a professor. At the conference, she was serving as co-chair of the Contact Group on Risk Assessment and Risk Management of Living Modified Organisms.

The Secretariat described her as a respected colleague whose expertise, leadership and commitment had contributed to the Convention and its protocols, as well as to the global biosafety community. It extended condolences to her family, friends, colleagues, the Namibian government and people, and the African Group and others mourning her death.

The Secretariat said it was working with the conference presidency to support Kandawa-Schulz’s family and the Namibian delegation and to make the necessary arrangements. A book of condolences was to be available to delegates from 13:00 on Monday at Entrance 2, near the Asia-Pacific Room. The circumstances of her death were not stated; reports indicated that she collapsed during a working group meeting on Friday.

CBD COP17 is being held in Yerevan, where governments and other participants are discussing biodiversity conservation and implementation of the Convention and its protocols. The conference includes government representatives, scientists, civil society representatives and researchers from nearly 196 countries.

title: Tinubu mourns Okonjo-Iweala’s mother
summary: President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the Okonjo family following the death of Kamene Okonjo, mother of WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, at 96.
body:
President Bola Tinubu has extended his heartfelt condolences to the Okonjo royal family of Ogwashi-Uku in Delta State on the passing of Professor Kamene Okonjo, who was the mother of Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, the Director-General of the World Trade Organization. Kamene Okonjo passed away at the age of 96. In a statement released by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu hailed the late scholar as a champion of women’s empowerment and a revered matriarch in her community.

In his statement, President Tinubu described her legacy as one of intellectual distinction and service to humanity, highlighting her commitment to advancing women and society at large. He expressed his sorrow over her death, emphasizing the loss not only to her family but also to the community of Ogwashi-Uku, where she was known as a beloved mother, matriarch, and community leader.

Kamene Okonjo was a distinguished sociologist recognized for her significant contributions to the understanding of the political and social roles of Igbo women, particularly west of the River Niger. Her influential works, such as the essay "The Dual-Sex Political System in Operation: Igbo Women and Community Politics in Midwestern Nigeria" published in 1976, remains widely referenced within African gender studies. Additionally, her 1980 work, "The Role of Women in Social Change among the Igbo of Southeastern Nigeria Living West of the River Niger," further exemplifies her scholarly impact.

She was married to Chukwuka Okonjo, who served as both a mathematician and economist, eventually becoming the Obi of Ogwashi-Uku in 2007 before his passing in 2019. The couple had seven children, among whom Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is the most prominent, having served as Nigeria’s Minister of Finance and as the former Managing Director of the World Bank.

Notably, Kamene Okonjo was also a victim of a high-profile kidnapping in 2012, a harrowing event linked to political tensions during her daughter's tenure in government. President Tinubu's heartfelt remarks serve to honor her legacy, and he prayed for her eternal rest while offering comfort to the grieving family and community.

title: Ebola: Day pandemic killed an Aláàfin, By Festus Adedayo
summary: Historical accounts reveal that a pandemic known as Pẹhẹ killed Supreme Monarch Aláàfin Májòótú in 1831, an enduring reminder of public health complacency.
body:
In 1831, a devastating pandemic known as Pẹhẹ claimed the life of Aláàfin Májòótú in Ọyọ-Ilé, highlighting the dire consequences of public health neglect. Historical records indicate that this highly contagious respiratory disease emerged unexpectedly, leading to swift fatalities across the Old Oyo Empire. The tragedy of Aláàfin's death signifies that plagues do not spare even the highest social echelons, a sentiment echoed in traditional Yoruba beliefs about the indiscriminate nature of death.

The pandemic, described in detail by the renowned historian Samuel Johnson, evolved from a local health issue to a widespread crisis by 1831, culminating in the downfall of the sacred palace. As Pẹhẹ spread, it wreaked havoc not only on the populace but also on the political stability of the empire. Alongside a severe famine and ongoing civil strife, the outbreak exacerbated the empire's existing struggles, leading to the deaths of thousands, including many who succumbed due to starvation rather than the disease itself.

Richard Lander, the Cornish explorer, documented the empire's attempts to manage the outbreak, noting the establishment of quarantine measures outside the city. However, the combination of Pẹhẹ with famine and political instability left the local authorities overwhelmed. By the time the pandemic waned, over 100,000 inhabitants had perished from the combined toll of disease and socio-political turmoil.

The historical narrative surrounding Pẹhẹ serves as a poignant reminder of the critical importance of vigilance in public health. As modern societies face similar challenges, the lessons from the past underscore the risk of complacency in managing health crises. The tragedy of Ọyọ-Ilé during this period illustrates how the mismanagement of a public health emergency can have lasting impacts on a nation’s socio-political fabric, potentially leading to its downfall. This ongoing relevance is particularly critical in light of contemporary health challenges, such as the recent Ebola case reported in Abuja, urging authorities to respond without delay.

title: ‘Filled with content creators’ — Bwala disparages NDC campaign council list
summary: Daniel Bwala criticized the NDC's National Campaign Council, calling it 'filled with content creators' and accusing it of hiding media surrogate identities.
body:
Daniel Bwala, a special adviser to President Bola Tinubu, has publicly criticized the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) for its recently unveiled National Campaign Council for the upcoming 2027 elections. He described the council as being 'filled with content creators' and alleged that the NDC is hiding the identities of its media surrogates within mainstream media. 

Bwala made these remarks on social media shortly after the NDC announced its campaign council, which aims to coordinate campaign activities and mobilize support for the party's candidates in the lead-up to the elections. The NDC has designated Senator Henry Seriake Dickson as the chairman of the council, with Peter Obi, the party's presidential candidate, serving as co-chairman. Other notable appointments include Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe as vice-chairman and Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso as co-vice-chairman, alongside Barrister Ikenna Morgan Enekweizu as council secretary and Mallam Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim as director-general.

The NDC has outlined its intentions to provide strategic leadership and promote a campaign that is centered on the people and issues rather than personality. They aim to foster unity among their members and supporters as the 2027 elections approach. Bwala's comments, made during a period of heightened political activity, reflect ongoing competition and scrutiny among the nation's political parties as they finalize their operational frameworks for the elections.

title: Opebi-Mende-Ojota Link Bridge To Be Opened Before Christmas, Says Sanwo-Olu
summary: Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu announced that the Opebi-Mende Link Bridge is 80% complete and will be opened before Christmas.
body:
Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has confirmed that the construction of the Opebi-Mende Link Bridge is approximately 80% complete. He expressed confidence that the bridge will be opened to the public before Christmas, despite the project exceeding its original September completion timeline.

During a recent site inspection, Governor Sanwo-Olu acknowledged the reasons for the delay while emphasizing the importance of maintaining the project's unique architectural and engineering standards. He highlighted the bridge's steel framework, which is designed to evoke the region's historical connection to cane weaving, thus ensuring cultural preservation in its design.

The construction involves the installation of over 300 tonnes of steel at heights reaching up to 25 meters. Governor Sanwo-Olu reported that three out of four major steel components have been completed, while work continues on the final component. Additionally, the bridge will feature light-emitting diode installations in the colours of Lagos State, enhancing its visual appeal.

Despite the setbacks, the governor reassured that the quality of engineering and public safety would remain a priority over speed. Once completed, the bridge will undergo site cleaning, kerb repainting, restoration of affected areas, and landscaping before it opens.

This infrastructure project, commissioned in 2022, aims to alleviate traffic congestion in Ikeja and surrounding areas. Governor Sanwo-Olu anticipates that the bridge will not only ease transportation but will also become a hub for recreation, culture, and tourism, enriching community identity and history. He views it as a significant addition to Lagos' infrastructure landscape, merging innovation with cultural significance.

title: It’s dangerous to buy Christmas clothes without paying tithes – cleric
summary: Pastor David Ibiyeomie warns Christians to prioritize tithes over Christmas spending, linking financial neglect to misfortunes. He urges correct tithe payments.
body:
Pastor David Ibiyeomie, founder of Salvation Ministries, expressed concern over the practice of tithing among Christians, particularly as the Christmas season approaches. In a recent sermon that gained attention on social media, he cautioned believers against overlooking their tithe commitments, stressing that they should not purchase festive clothing or gifts before fulfilling this religious duty.

Ibiyeomie articulated that neglecting tithes could lead to various misfortunes, which some might wrongly attribute to spiritual attacks. He recounted personal experiences involving vehicle breakdowns that he claims were linked to drivers’ failure to pay their tithes. One incident he described involved a burst tyre during a journey, which he attributed to the driver’s alleged lack of tithing. Similarly, he mentioned an instance concerning a driver of his Rolls-Royce, again citing burst tyres as proof of the consequences tied to unpaid tithes.

The pastor's message highlighted the belief that financial tribulations should not immediately be placed at the feet of the devil, promoting a more introspective approach to one’s religious obligations. He emphasized the importance of accuracy in tithe calculation and warned against casual approaches that allow individuals to contribute what they deem fit rather than what is deemed correct.

Ibiyeomie went further to implore Christians to take tithing seriously, especially during the festive season. He warned that neglecting this practice could have adverse effects on their families, hinting at potential dangers associated with not adhering to one's spiritual responsibilities. His statements challenge believers to critically assess their commitments and seek to align their actions with their faith, rather than attributing life’s challenges solely to external forces.

title: NDC Unveils Campaign Council, Names Dickson, Obi, Kwankwaso As Members
summary: The Nigeria Democratic Congress has established its campaign council for the 2027 elections, with key figures including Dickson, Obi, and Kwankwaso in leadership roles.
body:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has officially formed its national campaign council in anticipation of the 2027 general elections. The announcement was made on Sunday, revealing Senator Seriake Dickson as the chairman of the council. In prominent leadership positions, the NDC's presidential candidate, Peter Obi, serves as co-chairman, while the vice-presidential candidate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, acts as co-vice chairman.

In addition to Dickson, other notable members of the council include Senator Cleopas Zuwoghe, who is appointed as vice chairman, and former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Babachir Lawal, who will serve on the National Campaign Advisory Council. The campaign council includes various individuals tasked with different roles, highlighting a broad organizational strategy aimed at galvanizing support for the party's agenda.

The NDC has also outlined the formation of a 40-member national campaign advisory council and appointed 37 state campaign coordinators to streamline efforts across Nigeria. Key appointed roles include Osa Director as Director of Communication and Media, and retd. Major General John Enenche as Director of Security and Intelligence, emphasizing a commitment to a focused and secure campaign environment.

In its official communication, the NDC expressed a strong commitment to providing strategic leadership, coordinating campaign activities nationwide, and mobilizing support behind its vision for a 'new, just, and prosperous Nigeria.' The council aims to cultivate unity among party members and appeal to well-meaning Nigerians as a collective effort to address the country's challenges. This development is significant as it sets the foundation for the party's strategic approach in the upcoming elections.

title: The odds against Tinubu, By Wole Olaoye
summary: Bola Ahmed Tinubu remains a strong contender in Nigeria's upcoming presidential elections, but potential opposition unification poses a significant challenge.
body:
As Nigeria approaches its next presidential elections, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is considered a leading candidate, bolstered by control over the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). Despite his incumbency, there are significant challenges ahead, primarily stemming from the potential for a strategic coalition among major opposition figures, including Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi. 

If opposition candidates can unite around a single consolidated ticket, they could effectively pool their voting bases, significantly amplifying their chances against Tinubu. This coalition has the potential to cover key demographic areas, such as the South-East and South-South regions, urban centers, and strongholds in the North. In the previous election, the split opposition vote among various parties diluted their impact, highlighting the necessity for a unified front to challenge the current power dynamics.

However, forming such a coalition is fraught with challenges, chiefly the question of who will lead the ticket. Atiku, the seasoned veteran, may alienate Obi's supporters if he heads the campaign, while placing Obi in the lead could provoke resistance from traditional political elites in the North. Both factions have their vested interests, and the reluctance to compromise could thwart efforts to establish a viable opposition coalition. The internal discord among state-level party factions further complicates these negotiations, where local rivalries may impede larger strategic goals. 

Additionally, the political landscape is influenced by ethnic and regional dynamics, which can affect alliances and voter loyalty. Both the Yoruba and Igbo populations have seen attempts to incite division among them, underscoring the importance of unity among opposition constituents.

In light of these complexities, the opposition must either come together cohesively to present a compelling alternative or risk remaining fragmented and ineffective in the face of the formidable Tinubu and his ruling party. Time is running short, with less than three months until the elections, necessitating swift and decisive action to reshape Nigeria's political fabric.

title: U-17 Women’s World Cup: 3 African countries qualify for Round of 16 [Full list]
summary: Nigeria, Ghana, and Morocco advance to the Round of 16 in the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. They are among 16 teams proceeding in the tournament.
body:
Three African nations—Nigeria, Ghana, and Morocco—have successfully qualified for the Round of 16 in the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, hosted in Morocco. This achievement highlights the growing presence and competitiveness of African football on the global stage.

The tournament showcases some of the best young women’s football teams from around the world, and the inclusion of these three teams in the knockout stage underscores their determination and talent. These teams are set to compete against a diverse field that includes several strong contenders such as Germany, Japan, China, Spain, and the United States, among others.

The advancement of Nigeria, Ghana, and Morocco not only marks a significant milestone for these countries but also strengthens Africa’s representation in international women's football. As they compete for a spot in the quarter-finals, their performances will be pivotal in demonstrating the continent's potential in the sport.

As the tournament progresses, fans will be keen to follow how these teams fare against their adversaries in the knockout rounds. The success in reaching this stage reflects the ongoing development of women's football within Africa and aims to inspire further growth and investment in the sport on the continent.

title: El Clásico: Mbappé scores brace as Madrid Beat Barcelona 2-1
summary: Kylian Mbappé scored twice, leading Real Madrid to a 2-1 victory over Barcelona, halting the latter's unbeaten start to the season.
body:
In a much-anticipated El Clásico on Sunday, Real Madrid triumphed over FC Barcelona with a score of 2-1, marking a significant development in the La Liga title race. Kylian Mbappé was the standout player, scoring both goals for Real Madrid and showcasing his crucial role in the team's success.

The match kicked off with intense energy as both teams fought to assert dominance early on. Mbappé opened the scoring just before halftime in the 41st minute, converting after a defensive blunder from a Barcelona player allowed the ball to fall into his path. This goal put Real Madrid ahead, setting the stage for a competitive second half.

Barcelona responded strongly after the break, with their captain Raphinha equalizing in the 61st minute. His goal momentarily lifted the spirits of the home crowd as the Catalan side sought to preserve their unbeaten start to the league season at nine matches.

However, the match turned once again when Mbappé netted his second goal in the 87th minute. A well-timed assist from substitute Eduardo Camavinga ensured that Mbappé had a clear opportunity to score, and he did not miss, solidifying the victory for Real Madrid.

This result is particularly significant for Barcelona, which was aiming to extend their unbeaten streak to ten matches—a feat unmatched by any team so far in this season's competition. For Real Madrid, the victory is a crucial boost in their pursuit of the La Liga title, as they strive to close the gap on their rivals at the top of the table. Mbappé’s performance not only underlined his value to the team but also the enduring competitive spirit between these two historic clubs.

title: Real Madrid beat Barcelona 2-1 in La Liga Clasico
summary: Real Madrid defeated Barcelona 2-1 in a recent Clasico, with Kylian Mbappe scoring both goals, marking Barcelona's first domestic loss this season.
body:
In a closely contested La Liga Clasico on October 25, 2026, Real Madrid emerged victorious against Barcelona with a score of 2-1 at Camp Nou. Kylian Mbappe was the star of the match, scoring both goals for the visitors, while Raphinha found the net for Barcelona, who suffered their first domestic defeat of the season.

The match commenced with a cautious opening period, where both teams struggled to create clear scoring opportunities. Real Madrid made adjustments after losing their winger Vinicius Junior to suspension and fielded goalkeeper Andriy Lunin, who stepped in for the ill Thibaut Courtois. Despite Barcelona’s efforts, including chances from new signing Anthony Gordon, it was Mbappe who opened the scoring just before half-time. Taking advantage of an error from Barcelona defender Gerard Martin, he deflected a cross into the net, marking his tenth goal of the league season.

In the second half, Barcelona equalized shortly after the hour mark, with Raphinha scoring through the legs of Jude Bellingham after a well-timed pass from Pedri. This goal seemed to spark a resurgence in Barcelona’s attacking momentum, with players like Lamine Yamal and Martin making threatening runs towards the Real Madrid goal. However, Lunin kept Real Madrid in the game with crucial saves, particularly against Martin's header from a corner.

As the match progressed, it appeared that Barcelona might take control, but a decisive moment came late in the match. Substitute Gabriel Jesus lost the ball, allowing Real Madrid to counter quickly. Eduardo Camavinga's assist to Mbappe resulted in the Frenchman scoring his second goal into an empty net, sealing the victory for Los Blancos. This win marks Real Madrid's fifth consecutive victory across all competitions, while Barcelona, who had previously won their first nine league matches, is now facing a challenging period following two consecutive losses, including their Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain.

This Clasico result has significant implications for La Liga standings, as Real Madrid now closes the gap on league leaders Barcelona, making this match one of great importance in the title race.

title: Does Nigeria truly have over 103 million voters?, By Chidi Anselm Odinkalu
summary: Nigeria's electoral challenges persist as questions arise about the credibility of its voter registration numbers, especially ahead of the 2027 elections.
body:
As Nigeria prepares for its general elections in January and February 2027, concerns mount regarding the integrity of its voter registration figures. While the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) asserts that there are over 103 million registered voters, analysts caution that this number may be inflated due to a lack of accurate demographic data. Reports indicate that voter turnout in the last election plummeted to a mere 26.7%, the lowest since Nigeria’s return to civilian rule in 1999, raising alarms about voter engagement and electoral integrity.

The historical context of voter turnout in Nigeria reveals a troubling trend. In 1999, the turnout was recorded at 52.3%, but this figure has steadily decreased over the years, with significant declines noted in successive elections. The turnout registered in 2023 represents a substantial decline from the 34.8% noted in 2019. Such trends indicate a growing disaffection among the electorate, compounded by complaints of 'voter apathy' prevalent in electoral discussions.

However, skepticism regarding the credibility of these numbers stems from the underlying issues within INEC's registration process. For instance, demographic records are flawed, with only 53% of births and a mere 10% of deaths officially recorded. This raises concerns over the accuracy of the electoral roll, leading to suspicions that many 'registered voters' could be deceased. INEC has previously struggled to update its register to reflect such realities due to the lack of reliable demographic data, emphasizing the urgent need for a proper demographic management system.

Further complicating the situation, Nigeria's population has more than doubled since 1999, yet the growth of the voter registration roll has not kept pace. This mismatch may signal potential systemic issues, including migration, civic disengagement, and administrative inefficiencies within INEC. A significant proportion of the current voter register might include deceased individuals, and there is a growing call for transparency and reliability in the electoral process to bolster public confidence.

As discussions around electoral reform intensify, it becomes increasingly clear that merely increasing the number of registered voters is insufficient without addressing the conditions that affect voter participation. With ongoing debates about voter integrity and electoral transparency, the upcoming elections will serve as a critical test for Nigeria’s democratic processes and for INEC's ability to manage a credible electoral register.

title: 20:24 Inability To Transmit 2023 Presidential Election Results Eroded Trust In INEC — Ex-REC Igini
summary: Mike Igini stated that INEC's failure to transmit 2023 presidential election results has diminished public trust in the commission. He calls for vigilance in future elections.
body:
In a recent interview, former resident electoral commissioner Mike Igini expressed concerns regarding the trustworthiness of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) following the 2023 presidential election. Igini highlighted that the commission's inability to transmit results for this election, despite the functioning of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS), has significantly eroded public confidence in its credibility.

Igini explained that while BVAS performed adequately during the elections, the failure to transmit the presidential election results, when results for the other two elections held on the same day were successfully sent, has led to a climate of distrust towards INEC. He indicated that this incident created a significant liability for the current leadership of the commission, stating, "What broke confidence...was the fact that there were three elections, same day; only one could not be transmitted, which was the presidential." He admitted that even he struggles to provide a clear explanation for the technical glitch that reportedly occurred.

Looking toward the future, Igini emphasized that the upcoming 2027 elections will serve as a crucial assessment of whether Nigerians can learn from the mistakes of the 2023 election. He characterized every election as a test, asserting that the next one will be pivotal for citizens to demonstrate their understanding and resolve regarding electoral integrity. "It will be a verdict on whether we, as a people, can learn from what has happened," he stated.

Furthermore, he urged Nigerian voters to remain vigilant during future elections, especially during the collation of votes, to ensure that their votes are protected. Igini reminded voters that their collective presence at polling units outweighs any attempts at compromise by electoral officials, reinforcing the notion that the power ultimately lies with the electorate. This situation underlines the ongoing challenges INEC faces in restoring public trust in the electoral process as Nigeria approaches its next round of elections.

title: Ebola: Lagos Intensifies Surveillance, Reassures Residents Of Preparedness
summary: Lagos reports no suspected Ebola cases. It is strengthening surveillance after Nigeria confirmed its first Bundibugyo virus case.
body:
The Lagos State Government says there are currently no suspected Ebola cases in the state and that it is strengthening surveillance and response preparations. The measures follow confirmation of Nigeria’s first case of the Bundibugyo virus in the Federal Capital Territory. The state urged residents and visitors to remain calm and rely on official information.

Through the Ministry of Health’s Directorate of Epidemiology, Biosecurity and Global Health, Lagos is increasing disease monitoring, public communication and community engagement. It is also working with agencies at points of entry, including Murtala Muhammed International Airport. A recent engagement at the airport involved its management, Port Health Services and other aviation and public health stakeholders, with discussions covering passenger screening, information sharing, infection prevention and emergency coordination.

The state is distributing information about Ebola symptoms, transmission and prevention. It says the disease is mainly spread through direct contact with the blood or other body fluids of a symptomatic infected person, contaminated materials or the bodies of people who have died from the disease. Contact with infected animals can also result in infection. Symptoms may appear between two and 21 days after exposure and include fever, weakness, headache, muscle pain, sore throat, vomiting, diarrhoea and abdominal pain; unexplained bleeding or bruising may occur in some cases.

Because early symptoms can resemble malaria and other common illnesses, the government advises people who feel unwell, particularly after possible exposure or travel from an area with active transmission, to seek prompt medical assessment. Under Lagos’s fever-management policy, a person with fever should have a malaria rapid diagnostic test before taking antimalarial medicines. Anyone concerned about possible Ebola exposure is urged to contact public health authorities before going to a healthcare facility. In Lagos, concerns can be reported through emergency numbers 112 or 767, or to the state health ministry’s directorate at 0802 316 9485. The state says it will continue monitoring developments and coordinating its preparedness efforts.

title: Police Probe Fatal Shooting Of Two Officers In Kogi
summary: Kogi police are investigating the deaths of two officers in a shooting at ASCO Camp, Ajaokuta. The case has been referred to the state criminal investigations department.
body:
The Kogi State Police Command has opened an investigation into a fatal shooting at ASCO Camp in Ajaokuta that left two serving officers dead. Police said the incident was reported at 11:04 p.m. and that the Divisional Police Officer for Ajaokuta led officers to the scene.

According to the command’s preliminary findings, Corporal Amos Yusuf, who was on night duty, shot his colleague, Corporal Grace Onimisi, and then shot himself. Both officers were taken to separate medical facilities, where they were pronounced dead. Their remains were placed in the mortuary at ASCO Hospital. Police said an AK-47 rifle and four spent cartridges were recovered at the scene.

The case has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department for further inquiries. Police said the circumstances and motive remain under investigation and that the command would not speculate about details that have not been established. The commissioner of police expressed condolences to the officers’ families, colleagues and loved ones; the command said it would issue verified updates as appropriate.

title: Wike’s scholarship beneficiary emerges ABUAD’s best Law graduate
summary: Scholarship recipient Nengi Donald Jaja has become ABUAD’s top law graduate, earning 12 awards. He says a 2017 Rivers State grant helped make it possible.
body:
Nengi Donald Jaja, who received a Rivers State Government scholarship in 2017, has been named the overall Best Graduating Student in Afe Babalola University’s College of Law. He says he also received 12 awards and was the college’s salutatorian, describing the result as the fulfilment of a goal he had set for himself as a child.

In a post on X, Jaja said the scholarship followed a performance at an event in December 2017. It was intended to fund his education through secondary school and university. A report published by Tribune that month said former Rivers State Governor Nyesom Wike awarded him a ₦40 million scholarship after he sang at a thanksgiving service in Port Harcourt.

Jaja said the support encouraged him to pursue academic achievement while retaining his ambition to become an R&B and soul artiste. He reported earning a 5.00 GPA in eight of his ten university semesters, with scores of 4.96 and 4.87 in the other two. Across his studies, he said, he received 69 As and two Bs, while also holding several leadership positions. He added that he had been the best Arts student in secondary school.

Jaja credited his family, friends and lecturers for supporting him, and said music by singer Tems helped him stay emotionally grounded. He also described himself as the first male student to achieve the College of Law distinction. His account highlights the role the state-funded award played in enabling his education, while his academic record and honours mark the outcome of his studies at ABUAD.

body:

The latest figure is four times the number initially confirmed by police. The source material does not provide further details about when the attack occurred, where in Taraba it took place or how the higher toll was established.

title: Real Madrid’s Courtois Out Of Clasico With Flu
summary: Real Madrid ruled Thibaut Courtois out of Sunday’s Clasico against Barcelona after he came down with flu. Andriy Lunin is expected to start.
body:
Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois will miss Sunday’s Clasico against Barcelona after falling ill with flu, the club announced a few hours before the match. Madrid described him as a last-minute withdrawal from the squad.

Ukrainian goalkeeper Andriy Lunin is set to replace Courtois against Barcelona, who are unbeaten under coach Hansi Flick. The match is at Camp Nou.

The absence adds to Madrid’s personnel problems for the game: winger Vinicius Junior is also unavailable because of suspension. Madrid are third in the league, six points behind leaders Barcelona, making the meeting significant to the title race.
